Pal. Regt. הובא למנוחות עולמים בבית הקברות הצבאי TEL AVIV (NAHLAT YITZHAK) CEMETERY, ישראל. מיקום הקבר: Plot 49. Row 13. Grave 7.
cvEn:
Yosef-Zadok Lindenwurm, son of Mordehai, was born in 5663 (1903) in Lublin, Poland. He was a member of the Poale Zion party and was among its activists when he moved to Warsaw. He was also active in the party's building workers' union and in the Arbeiterheim. In 1924 he immigrated to Eretz Israel with a group of members of the Borochov youth movement and settled in Tel Aviv. There he worked as a building laborer and married his partner, who had immigrated with the same group.

Yosef joined the Labor Battalion and worked in Kfar Gila'adi and in Haifa. When the Haifa company of the battalion was disbanded, he returned to Tel Aviv and continued working as a building laborer. Here too he was active in the Poale Zion branch, and he even headed the branch council. Later he joined the Mishmar companies of the Palestinian Infantry Corps and served at the Reading station in Tel Aviv.

On 20 Sivan 5705 (1 June 1945) he drowned in the sea off Tel Aviv. He left a wife. His name is commemorated in the *Sefer HaHitnadvut* (the Volunteers' Book) and in the *Yizkor* book of the Jabotinsky Institute.

Further details of his service in the British Army: Yosef Zadok Lindenwurm (Lindenwurm Zadok Joseph), British service number PAL/60008, enlisted in the British Army in 1942. He was posted to the British Infantry Corps (INF.) in the Buffs-100 unit. His British Army rank was Private (Pte.). He was later transferred to the Jewish Battalion, Palestine Regiment. He was laid to rest in the TEL AVIV (NAHLAT YITZHAK) CEMETERY military cemetery, Israel. Grave location: Plot 49, Row 13, Grave 7.
